title: Derived coefficient comparison with representative equation
statement: Let R,A,B,D be commutative rings with R-algebras A,B and an (A tensor_R B)-algebra D [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]. Let F:D(R) to D(B) with universal counit delta derive extension R to B, and let L:D(A) to D(D) with universal counit epsilon derive extension A to D [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For each integer i there exists a natural B-linear transformation from H^i(F(Res_R(M))) to Res_B H^i(L(M)). For every A-complex P and every B-linear chain map beta from B tensor_R Res_R(P) to Res_B(D tensor_A P) sending b tensor p to the image of 1 tensor b tensor p, its representative equation is H^i(F(c_P inverse);delta_P) followed by the homology localization factors, H^i(beta), and the successive D-to-(A tensor_R B) and (A tensor_R B)-to-B homology restriction isomorphisms, equals tau at Q(P) followed by restriction of the scalar-extension counit homology map. Here c_P is the quotient-to-derived restriction input isomorphism. No counit invertibility at P, flatness, cohomology model, transport e, or derived morphism a is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the natural comparison eta in the derived category, with its counit-compatible chain representative equation, before choosing a homology degree.

Whisker eta by degree-i homology and compose with the inverse of the exact restriction derived-homology natural isomorphism. Apply homology to the chain equation. Naturality and the evaluated derived-homology isomorphism give the required counit formula. The composition identity for restriction homology identifies the composite restriction map with the two successive maps written in the statement.
